headline: Sandiganbayan Commits Romualdez to Quezon City Jail Custody as Hospital Request Remains Pending
seoTitle: Court Commits Romualdez to Quezon City Jail Custody | FMB News
seoDescription: The Sandiganbayan issued a commitment order placing Martin Romualdez under BJMP custody for detention at New Quezon City Jail while his hospital-confinement request remains unresolved.
deck: The Sandiganbayan issued a commitment order designating New Quezon City Jail for former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, while the court continues to consider his request to remain confined at a private hospital.
author: FMB News Desk

continuesFrom.headline: Ombudsman Files Plunder Case Against Martin Romualdez Over Alleged Flood-Control Kickback Scheme
continuesFrom.whatChanged: Since FMB News first reported the Ombudsman filing, the Sandiganbayan found probable cause and ordered Romualdez's arrest. The court has now issued a commitment order designating New Quezon City Jail as his detention facility, while his request for continued hospital confinement remains before the court.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Sandiganbayan Third Division issued a commitment order on September 10 directing that former House Speaker and Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez be committed for detention at the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas, Quezon City, in connection with the pending ₱7.44-billion plunder case.

GMA News and Philstar.com separately reported the court order. The order places the accused under the detention framework of the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology, but it did not immediately resolve whether Romualdez would physically leave Cardinal Santos Medical Center, where he has remained confined while asking the court to allow continued hospital detention.

The court action is a custody and detention decision in an ongoing criminal case. It is not a finding that Romualdez committed plunder. The ₱7.44-billion amount is the amount alleged by prosecutors, and the criminal accusations remain unproven.

sections.heading: What changed since FMB's first report
paragraphs: FMB News first reported on September 7 that the Office of the Ombudsman had filed the plunder case. Later that day, the Sandiganbayan found probable cause, issued arrest warrants, and police served Romualdez his warrant while he was hospitalized.

The new development is the September 10 commitment order designating New Quezon City Jail as the detention facility. At the time of this report, the separate question of whether Romualdez may continue staying at Cardinal Santos Medical Center for medical reasons had not been finally resolved in the reporting reviewed by FMB News. The earlier reports remain intact as the historical record.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Office of the Ombudsman accuses Romualdez and three co-accused of receiving at least ₱7.44 billion in alleged commissions, kickbacks and other benefits connected to flood-control, infrastructure and other government projects funded from 2022 to 2025.

Romualdez has denied wrongdoing and has said through counsel that he will answer the allegations through the judicial process. His lawyers have asked the Sandiganbayan to allow him to remain at Cardinal Santos Medical Center while doctors assess medical conditions cited in his request for continued hospital confinement.

The Ombudsman has opposed continued detention at the private hospital and has argued that government medical facilities can evaluate and address his condition. The Sandiganbayan is responsible for determining the conditions of custody while the criminal case proceeds.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The case concerns allegations involving billions of pesos and government infrastructure spending, including flood-control projects that directly affect public safety and disaster resilience. Court decisions on custody are therefore part of a closely watched test of whether high-profile defendants are subjected to the same judicial process and detention rules as other accused persons.

The distinction between detention procedure and criminal guilt remains essential. A commitment order determines custody; it does not prove the prosecution's allegations. Guilt or innocence must be decided through the court process and evidence.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The immediate question is how the Sandiganbayan will rule on Romualdez's request for continued hospital confinement and when, if medically and legally cleared, he will be physically transferred to the detention facility designated by the court.

His arraignment is scheduled for September 14 according to Philstar.com. FMB News will also watch for further Sandiganbayan orders, official BJMP custody updates and filings from the prosecution and defense that materially change the case.

verificationNotes: The central event is verified by separate GMA News and Philstar.com reports describing the Sandiganbayan Third Division commitment order.
GMA News explicitly reported that the court had not yet ordered an immediate physical transfer from Cardinal Santos Medical Center when it published its report.
The article distinguishes the commitment order and custody arrangements from any finding of criminal guilt.
The ₱7.44-billion figure is identified as an amount alleged in the prosecution case, not as proven stolen funds or proven ill-gotten wealth.

This is a material continuation of FMB News' September 7 first report on the Ombudsman filing. The visible Continues from link points to that earliest relevant canonical FMB News article, not merely to the later arrest update.
The September 7 originals remain unchanged as historical reports.
